latest.title: ECR appoints Head of Australian Operations
latest.content:
15 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 7182U
ECR Minerals PLC
15 September 2026
REACH - non-regulatory announcement*
15 September 2026
ECR MINERALS PLC
("ECR Minerals", "ECR" or the "Company")
ECR appoints Head of Australian Operations
Mike McRae-Williams joins as Maddens approaches production phase
ECR Minerals plc (LON: ECR), the exploration and development company focused on gold in Australia, is pleased to announce the appointment of Mike McRae-Williams as Operations Manager for Australia, a non-Board management role.
Mike joins ECR following its acquisition of Paleogold, where he served as Exploration and Production Director, and brings approximately 35 years of mining industry experience together with extensive knowledge of the projects acquired by ECR through Paleogold.
His appointment comes at a pivotal stage for the Company as Maddens approaches its production phase and ECR increases operational activity across the wider Maddens Flat Group of Mines and its broader Australian portfolio. ECR has a 50% interest in the Maddens Flat Group of Mines.
Mike has worked closely with the Maddens Flat Group of Mines over a number of years and has detailed knowledge of the Maddens Underground Mine, processing infrastructure and operating team. He has previously contributed to upgrades to production and processing operations at Maddens and continues to play an active role in the preparation and optimisation of the processing circuit.
His experience also extends across the wider Maddens Flat Group of Mines, where ECR is evaluating additional opportunities including the Brothers and other historic workings across the project area. The Company expects Mike's combination of processing, metallurgical, underground and alluvial experience to be invaluable as activity increases across the broader Maddens Flat portfolio.
Mike also has detailed knowledge of the Salt Bush Gold Project in South Australia. He has been closely involved in developing the proposed work programme at Salt Bush, which is to include trenching, systematic sampling and metallurgical test work designed to improve understanding of the project as it progresses towards development. ECR owns 20% of the Salt Bush Gold Project.
Mike holds a Master of Science degree from the University of Melbourne and has extensive experience across project management, metallurgical assessment, process plant design, construction, commissioning and plant operations. During his career he has managed and designed gold processing operations ranging from underground mine treatment plants to large-scale tailings retreatment projects.
Mike also brings extensive alluvial gold experience, which the Company expects to apply across opportunities at the Brothers, Blue Mountain and potentially elsewhere within the Australian portfolio.
ECR Chairman Nick Tulloch commented
:
"Mike joins ECR at an important moment. As previously announced, Maddens is approaching its production phase and our priority is increasingly about operational execution on the ground.
"Few people know Maddens and the wider Paleogold portfolio as well as Mike. He has worked closely with the project and its processing infrastructure for several years and brings exactly the combination of practical mining, metallurgy and plant experience that we need as activity increases.
"Importantly, his skillset will be invaluable across the wider Maddens Flat Group of Mines, not just at the Maddens Underground Mine. As previously announced, we are already evaluating additional opportunities across the Brothers and the other historic workings, and Mike's knowledge of both hard-rock and alluvial operations gives us considerable flexibility as we seek to advance those projects.
"He also knows Salt Bush extremely well and brings valuable experience that can be applied across Blue Mountain and our other Australian opportunities.
"Mike already knows the projects, the people and the equipment. Bringing him into ECR on a senior management role provides continuity and additional operational leadership at exactly the point when we need it most."

latest.title: Maddens Development Advances Towards Production
latest.content:
14 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 5229U
ECR Minerals PLC
14 September 2026
The information contained within this announcement was deemed by the Company to constitute inside information as stipulated under the UK Market Abuse Regulation.
14 September 2026
ECR MINERALS PLC
("ECR Minerals", "ECR" or the "Company")
Maddens Decline Development Advances Towards Production
ECR Minerals plc (LON: ECR), the exploration and development company focused on gold in Australia, is pleased to announce that development drilling and blasting is now underway on the main decline (the downwards tunnel to access the ore body) at the Maddens Underground Mine in North Queensland, marking an important step in the Company's programme to commence gold production from Maddens during Q4 2026. ECR has a 50% interest in the Maddens Flat Group of Mines.
The commencement of decline advancement follows a significant programme of underground enabling works, including upgrades to mine ventilation, establishment of escapeways, surveying and preparation of underground equipment. In parallel, refurbishment of the existing processing plant is progressing, including installation of a 20-inch Knelson concentrator.
Highlights
·
Development drilling and blasting is now underway on the main decline of the Maddens Underground Mine from the 355m level.
·
Maddens has entered its next phase of underground development, following significant work already completed on ventilation, underground safety and access, surveys and equipment preparation.
·
Decline advancement of approximately 72.5m is targeting the development of an ore drive with approximately 12.5m of stoping height ("backs"), which is believed to contain an estimated potential of 1,500 oz Au.
·
Processing plant refurbishment advancing in parallel, including installation of a 20-inch Knelson concentrator to optimise gold recovery.
·
First ore processing from existing surface stockpiles is currently expected by the end of September 2026.
·
Gold production from newly accessed underground ore targeted during Q4 2026, as development advances towards the planned intersection with the Maddens Reef.
·
The current programme is intended to be an important step in establishing Maddens as a producing hard-rock gold operation within the wider Maddens Flat Group of Mines.
Background
Recent work at the Maddens Underground Mine has focused on upgrading the mine ventilation system, establishing escapeways from the decline face to surface, and conducting surveys and equipment preparation to enable decline advancement. From the 355m level, the decline is to advance 15m to the north-east, curve southwards for a 180-degree turn, and advance 37.5m south-west to a planned intersection of the Maddens Reef at approximately 342m (see Fig. 1). Some 12.5m of stoping height ("backs") is expected to be developed, containing an estimated potential of 1,500 oz of gold.
Fig 1. Maddens Mine viewed from the southwest. Note only accessible stopes surveyed.
Processing plant refurbishments are underway, including the installation of a 20-inch Knelson concentrator to optimise gold recovery. The first ore processing from existing surface stockpiles is expected by the end of September 2026.
ECR Non-Executive Director Mike Parker commented:
"With the ventilation upgrade completed and the key underground enabling work now in place, Maddens has moved into an important new phase. Development drilling and blasting on the main decline is underway, with the focus now firmly on advancing towards the next area of production ore.
"The planned decline development is designed to provide access to an ore drive with approximately 12.5 metres of stoping height and an estimated potential of 1,500 ounces of gold. Importantly, this work is being undertaken within an existing underground mine with established infrastructure, an experienced operating team and a processing plant already on site.
"Plant refurbishment is also progressing in parallel, including installation of the 20-inch Knelson concentrator. Our objective is to bring newly mined underground ore into production during Q4 2026, and I am very encouraged by the progress being made on site."
ECR Chairman Nick Tulloch added:
"Having visited the Maddens mine in recent days, it is clear that the team has made significant progress in advancing production capabilities across both the underground mine and the processing plant. Considerable work has already been completed on ventilation, rock bolting and escapeways, and we are now seeing that preparation translate into active decline development.
"We are excited to see the fruition of this hard work, with the mine advancing well and plant refurbishments underway that will enable ECR to report its maiden production from Maddens in the coming months. The next major objective is to access the planned production area through the decline, with production from newly mined underground ore targeted during Q4 2026.
"Maddens is an important part of the wider Maddens Flat Group of Mines and we are very encouraged by the progress being made on site. I would like to thank the team for their continued efforts and dedication."

Michael Parker has a BSc. in Mining Geology and is a professional geologist and is a Fellow of the Australasian Institute of Mining and Metallurgy (FAusIMM). He is a qualified person as defined by the AIM Note for Mining, Oil and Gas Companies.

latest.title: New soil results expand gold target at Lolworth
latest.content:
9 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 9236T
ECR Minerals PLC
09 September 2026
9 September 2026
ECR MINERALS PLC
("ECR Minerals", "ECR" or the "Company")
New soil results expand gold target at Lolworth
Strong gold anomalies identify broader structural system and new diamond core drill targets
ECR Minerals plc (AIM: ECR), the exploration and development company focused on gold in Australia, is pleased to announce highly encouraging results from its latest soil sampling programme at the Company's 100%-owned Lolworth Project in North Queensland, Australia ("Lolworth" or the "Project").
The latest soil sampling results provide important new evidence that the gold-bearing structural system previously identified through surface exploration and the Company's maiden drilling programme potentially extends significantly beyond the areas tested by drilling to date.
Highlights
·
31 soil samples returned gold values of 100 ppb Au or greater
, including a peak result of
608 ppb Au
.
·
Results support a
broader NNW-trending gold-bearing structural system
extending beyond the area tested by ECR's maiden RC drilling.
·
A
second parallel gold trend
has also been identified to the north-east of Uncle Terry.
·
Previous drilling confirmed shallow gold and silver mineralisation, including
2m @ 3.57 g/t Au
and
4m @ 7.18 g/t Ag
.
·
Results strengthen the case for a
broader diamond core drilling programme
to test the gold structures at depth and across their interpreted width.
·
The principal gold trend may extend south towards similarly orientated structures at
Gorge Creek West
.
Latest Soil Sampling Results
The Company has received the remaining 1,002 assay results from a broader test programme comprising approximately 1,500 soil samples collected across the Uncle Terry area.
The programme was designed to test for gold together with associated pathfinder elements and, importantly, to assess whether structures previously interpreted from field mapping and rock-chip sampling could potentially be identified beneath areas of surface cover.
Ground conditions at Uncle Terry include areas which are obscured by high grass for substantial periods of the year, in-turn limiting the effectiveness of conventional surface mapping. Soil geochemistry therefore provides an important additional tool for tracing mineralised structures where outcrop is limited.
Of the latest results,
31 samples returned gold values of 100 ppb Au or greater
, which the Company's geological team considers to be a strong anomaly. The highest individual result was
608 ppb Au
(see summary of soil samples in Table One).
Figure One: Plan of Uncle Terry showing reported soil Au results, previous drilling and interpreted structural trends
Improved Geological Interpretation
The Board considers that the latest soil results materially refine ECR's geological interpretation of the Uncle Terry area.
The principal
NNW-trending structure is interpreted to be gold-bearing
, while the
NE-trending shear sets show a stronger association with silver mineralisation
.
The initial RC drilling was largely focused on these NE structures, meaning that the main NNW gold trend has not yet been comprehensively drill tested.
The soil results are also interpreted as defining a
second parallel NNW-trending gold anomaly
to the north-east, where previous mapping identified gold-bearing quartz stringer veins.
Importantly, the interpreted main NNW gold structure can be projected further south towards similarly orientated structures mapped at
Gorge Creek West
, supporting the potential for a broader mineralised system.
Previous Drilling
ECR completed its maiden RC drilling programme at Lolworth during 2025, comprising
28 holes for an aggregate 1,058 metres
across the Uncle Terry and Gorge Creek West prospects.
The programme successfully demonstrated shallow gold and silver mineralisation, details of which were announced on 1 December 2025.
Notable gold intercepts included:
·
2m @ 3.57 g/t Au from 14m
- LWDR012, Uncle Terry;
·
1m @ 2.04 g/t Au from 21m
- LWDR026, Gorge Creek West;
·
1m @ 1.44 g/t Au from 7m
- LWDR011, Uncle Terry; and
·
5m @ 0.47 g/t Au from 14m
- LWDR025, Gorge Creek West.
Notable silver intercepts included:
·
4m @ 7.18 g/t Ag from 33m
- LWDR006, Uncle Terry;
·
1m @ 15.0 g/t Ag from 11m
- LWDR021, Uncle Terry;
·
1m @ 10.1 g/t Ag from 14m
- LWDR012, Uncle Terry; and
·
4m @ 3.33 g/t Ag from 14m
- LWDR025, Gorge Creek West.
These results established the presence of a shallow gold-silver mineralised system. The latest soil programme now indicates that the structural extent of the gold system is broader than the area tested by that initial drilling.
Next Steps
The Company's geological team will incorporate the new soil geochemistry into the existing structural model for Uncle Terry and Gorge Creek West.
On the basis of the results received to date, ECR considers that a
broader diamond core drilling programme is warranted to test the interpreted NNW gold-bearing structures at depth and across their full width
.
A potential future drilling programme would be designed to test:
·
the principal NNW gold-bearing structure at Uncle Terry;
·
the newly identified parallel NNW gold trend to the north-east;
·
the relationship between the NNW gold structures and the NE-trending silver-bearing shears; and
·
the potential southern continuation of the mineralised system towards Gorge Creek West.
Further details of the potential exploration programme will be provided as planning progresses.
ECR Chief Geologist Adam Jones commented
:
"These results significantly strengthen our understanding of the gold system at Uncle Terry. Our initial drilling in 2025 confirmed shallow gold and silver mineralisation, and the latest soil results now indicate a broader NNW-trending gold structure as well as a second parallel gold trend to the north-east.
"Importantly, these structures have not yet been fully tested by drilling. The next step would be a broader diamond core drilling programme to test the gold system at depth and across its interpreted width, including its potential continuation towards Gorge Creek West."
ECR Chairman Nick Tulloch added:
"These are highly encouraging results from Lolworth and, importantly, they tell us considerably more than simply where gold is present in the soil.
"ECR considers that our maiden drilling programme established that we have a gold-silver mineralised system at Lolworth. What this latest work is now indicating is that the gold component of that system may be considerably broader than the area that we initially drilled, which is an exciting development for the Project.
"Lolworth covers 946 square kilometres, including a significant amount of highly prospective ground and remains one of the largest exploration opportunities within ECR's portfolio. We have always recognised its potential scale, but as our geological understanding improves, we are beginning to identify increasingly defined structures and clearer targets across the Project.
"The identification of two NNW-trending gold anomalies, alongside the previously established silver-bearing structures, gives us a much stronger geological framework for the next phase of exploration. We are very encouraged by what these results are showing, and we look forward to continuing to build our understanding of the wider potential at Lolworth."
Review of Announcement by Qualified Person
This announcement has been reviewed by
Adam Jones, Chief Geologist at ECR Minerals Plc
. Adam Jones is a professional geologist and a Member of the Australian Institute of Geoscientists (MAIG). He is a qualified person as that term is defined by the AIM Note for Mining, Oil and Gas Companies.

latest.title: New quartz reef with visible gold at Maddens
latest.content:
8 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 8365T
ECR Minerals PLC
08 September 2026
The information contained within this announcement was deemed by the Company to constitute inside information as stipulated under the UK Market Abuse Regulation.
8 September 2026
ECR MINERALS PLC
("ECR Minerals", "ECR" or the "Company")
New quartz reef with visible gold at Maddens
Jack's Reef adds significant new exploration potential
ECR Minerals plc (LON: ECR), the exploration and development company focused on gold in Australia, is pleased to announce the identification of a new visible gold-bearing quartz reef at the Maddens Mine in the Maddens Gold Project in North Queensland ("Maddens"). ECR has a 50% interest in Maddens.
The newly recognised reef, named "Jack's Reef", was encountered during underground development work associated with ventilation infrastructure at the Maddens Mine.
The Board considers this to be particularly important, because Jack's Reef may indicate a key geological model linking the existing historic Maddens Mine workings and potential extensions of the broader mineralised system.
Highlights
·
New visibly gold-bearing reef discovered underground at the Maddens Mine, encountered during development works.
·
Jack's Reef is a consistent quartz structure, approximately 50 centimetres or more in width in places, with clearly visible gold observed within parts of the exposed reef.
·
Potential geological model: the position of Jack's Reef may explain why mineralisation appears to terminate at the northern end of the mine and could indicate a continuation or change in orientation of the existing Maddens Mine mineralised system due to structural controls.
·
New exploration opportunity: the discovery potentially opens up additional ground around the existing mine and towards the known Maddens Northern Lode for targeted exploration.
·
Existing mine infrastructure provides an important advantage, allowing the Company to investigate Jack's Reef from active underground workings rather than relying solely on surface exploration.
·
Production imminent: a significant amount of material from Jack's Reef is already stockpiled on surface, with processing activity expected to commence later this month.
Jack's Reef Discovery
Jack's Reef was encountered during development of an underground rise for the ventilation system at the Maddens Mine at the northern limit of the known mineralisation.
The reef is a consistent quartz structure, constrained within host-rock foliation, approximately 50 centimetres or more in width in places, with visible gold regularly observed within the quartz (see Fig 1. below). The exposed vertical extent of the reef is approximately 10 m in the rise and 5- 10 m along strike.
Fig. 1: Hand specimen from Jack's Reef showing visible gold (ringed)
Jack's Reef is considered particularly significant because of its locality and geological characteristics.
Recent three-dimensional surveying of the historic Maddens Mine workings shows that the existing mineralisation appears to terminate close to the area where Jack's Reef begins. The Maddens Mine's mineralisation mined to date cross-cuts host-rock foliation by about 30 degrees, whereas Jack's Reef follows foliation. Underground examination and surface exposures indicate that the Maddens Mine's mineralisation broadly changes bearing by 30 degrees clockwise at the northern end of the underground mine workings and becomes foliation-parallel over several horizons. The major manifestation of this orientation change is Jack's Reef. This form of structure is known as a "ramp and flat", where the structures "ramp" across foliation (as seen in the current Maddens Mine) and then exploit foliation-parallel weaknesses ("flats", or Jack's Reef) to propagate further. The Jack's Reef flat trends towards the Maddens Northern Lode and, although poorly exposed at only one site, appears to connect the Maddens Mine and the Maddens Northern Lode (see Fig, 2). The Maddens Northern Lode, a site of known mineralisation with significant historic underground workings, "ramps" (cross-cuts) foliation again, until a northern flat splay can be traced by pitting carried out by previous operators.
Fig. 2: Plan view of Maddens Ramp-Flat structure under 2026 Lidar imagery. Old workings indicated by Lidar confirmed by field visits.

The south end of Maddens Mine also shows characteristics of entering into a flat. The North Flat has yet to be explored in any detail. All structures dip moderately to steeply west to south-west. The Board considers that the presence of ramp and flat structures at Maddens should significantly increase the exploration potential. In compressional structural regimes such as the Maddens project area, ramp-to-flat transitions create "dilatant" zones that can trigger gold deposition due to pressure drops and fracturing; at the same sites, permeability zones can form, with increased potential for high grades. Whilst mineralisation is not yet confirmed to be continuous across the whole system, the potential focus of high-grade zones at ramp-to-flat interfaces is considered by the Board to be a significant exploration advance, not only for the Maddens Mine but across the whole exploration tenement.
If confirmed through further work, the Board considers that this could materially increase the geological opportunity around the existing mine by demonstrating that gold-bearing structures continue beyond areas previously thought to represent the limits of historic development.
Jack's Reef gives ECR the opportunity to investigate potential additional mineralised areas at the Maddens Mine by targeted follow-up work from underground and/or a potential focused surface drill program. Such mineralised areas, if confirmed by continuity, thickness, and grade, could be accessed by stoping from current mine infrastructure with little additional development required.
The wider Maddens project tenements contain a number of historic mines and workings, and until now, there has been limited modern, systematic exploration to understand how these structures may be connected.
The identification of Jack's Reef therefore provides a potentially important new piece of the geological model and may help the Company build a clearer picture of the scale and continuity of the broader mineralised system.
Future Exploration Potential
The Company intends to continue to investigate Jack's Reef and undertake targeted follow-up work to better understand its orientation, continuity of dimensions and grade, and relationship with the existing Maddens Mine reef system.
This work will also consider whether similar structures may exist elsewhere around the historic mine area.
The Board believes the combination of visible gold, the consistent nature of the reef, its position relative to the existing workings, and the wider historic mineralisation across the Maddens project tenements creates a compelling opportunity for further exploration alongside ongoing mine development.
ECR Non-Executive Director Mike Parker commented
:
"Jack's Reef is one of the most exciting geological developments we have seen recently at Maddens. Not only does it form part of a much more extensive vein system than previously thought, but the ramp and flat structures form an excellent model for targeted high-grade delineation in the existing mines and for exploration models tenement-wide. The Maddens Mine appears to be on the same structure as Maddens Northern Lode, and where the ramp-flat interface occurs at the Northern Lode is a site of extensive previous mining on reportedly high-grades - exactly where the model predicts. We consider that the Maddens Northern Lode, as part of the main Maddens structure, can now be regarded as much more prospective, potentially to a similar extent as the Maddens Mine itself.
The Maddens Mine is already a highly prospective historic gold mine, but the discovery of Jack's Reef demonstrates why we believe there could be considerably more opportunity around the existing workings than has previously been recognised. Translating this structural model, and others we are developing, to the broader Maddens project tenements and other mine sites may reveal the true potential of the area, which formed part of our decision to acquire our 50% interest in this highly prospective, yet underexplored, project."
ECR Chairman Nick Tulloch added
:
"Jack's Reef is very encouraging and adds another dimension to the opportunity at the Maddens project.
"The presence of visible gold is clearly exciting, but just as importantly, the location and substantial nature of the reef may help us better understand how the mineralised system continues beyond the historic workings.
"This is exactly the type of finding we hoped the recent underground work and survey programme would begin to identify.
"Alongside this exploration upside, our immediate operational focus remains firmly on moving Maddens into production. A significant amount of material from both Jack's Reef and the main Maddens Mine is already stockpiled on surface and we expect processing activity to commence this month.
"We therefore have the combination of near-term production activity and a potentially important new geological opportunity developing at the same project."

company_30s.what_they_do: ECR Mining is a junior gold exploration and development company based in Western Australia.  It owns and works on several gold projects – the Maddens mine, the Creswick Gold Project and the Tuckanarra project – and focuses on drilling, mapping and early‑stage development to bring those sites to production.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Gold remains a key hedge for investors and a source of income for mining companies worldwide.  ECR’s projects sit in a prolific gold‑bearing region, and the company’s ability to turn a quartz reef into a production pipeline could add significant value to the sector, especially as commodity demand stays strong.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is still in the exploration and early development phase, having recently raised small amounts of capital through share placements and farm‑in agreements.  Cash burn is high, but the company has secured new funding and is actively drilling to confirm gold presence.

rns_narrative: ECR announced a new quartz reef with visible gold at the Maddens site, giving the project a tangible target for future drilling.
The company has secured farm‑in and joint‑venture agreements for the Creswick Gold Project, reducing its equity stake and bringing in experienced partners.
A series of smaller announcements – from a new drill target at Lolworth to the latest half‑yearly results – show that management is keeping momentum and trying to keep investors informed.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet skepticism punctuated by hopeful bursts when new drilling results surface.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of traders point to the quartz reef and the farm‑in deals as evidence that the company is moving toward production and that a bounce could be imminent.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Many voices caution that the firm still needs a proven gold source and that cash burn could outpace new funding, putting the company at risk of stalling or falling further.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter is low but not negative; it has shifted from pure doubt to cautious optimism whenever a new drill result or funding announcement appears.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends is flat – there is no public buzz, giving a contrarian edge.

near_term_catalysts: A scheduled RNS on the results of the first drilling campaign at the Maddens quartz reef – a positive result could confirm gold presence.
Any announcement of additional share placement or a new farm‑in agreement that reduces cash burn.
A breakout from the current support level if volume spikes, suggesting that traders are stepping in after the deep sell‑off.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a 10‑15% jump in daily volume, a price bounce to the 50‑day moving average, or a clear statement from management that the first drilling round is complete.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock sits in the early stage of a crash‑recovery cycle: the APEX score signals tight compression, which often precedes a breakout.  The next few weeks are critical – a single positive announcement or a volume spike could trigger the mean‑reversion we expect.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The company is deeply discounted after a sharp sell‑off, yet it has a tangible gold target and new funding to keep the project alive.  If the first drilling round confirms gold, the price could climb back to roughly the middle of its 52‑week range – a 70‑plus percent upside from today’s level.  The historical record for deep crashes shows that the best rewards come from these long‑term rebounds.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: ECR still faces a high cash burn and has not yet produced any gold.  If the drilling fails or the company cannot raise additional capital, the price could fall further, potentially to zero if the project is abandoned.  The worst case is a total loss of invested capital.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside: ~70% from current price to the midpoint of the 52‑week range.  Immediate downside risk: a 10‑15% drop in the next week would wipe out the margin of safety.  The risk‑reward ratio is therefore roughly 7:1 – a strong asymmetry for a contrarian play.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a pullback to the 20‑day moving average, size the position to 5% of the portfolio, and set a stop 5% below that support level.  Use the high APEX score as a confirmation that a breakout is likely.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash until you see a volume spike of at least 10% over the 20‑day average and the price touches the 50‑day moving average.  These are clear signs that traders are starting to take positions after the deep sell‑off.
playbook.if_passing: There are no imminent delisting or bankruptcy signals.  The only terminal risk would be a complete loss of the project’s viability, which would be obvious from a new negative RNS.

ai_insights.bottom_line: ECR sits at a deep crash, has fresh drilling prospects and tight compression – a contrarian bullish set‑up with a 70% upside if the company turns its latest quartz reef into a production pipeline, offering a 7:1 risk‑reward profile.
